proposals.note: Designed a block with high symmetry to match the graph connectivity task. The block consists of uniform single-qubit rotations (RX, RY, RZ) on all 6 qubits, followed by a cycle of CZ gates connecting neighbors in a ring topology (0-1-2-3-4-5-0). The hypothesis claims invariance under the dihedral group D6 (generated by rotation and reflection), which is a subgroup of the full S6 symmetry of the graph problem. This symmetry reduction helps the model generalize to any graph isomorphism class while keeping the parameter count low (3 params) and dev risk low by avoiding overfitting to specific node indices. The CZ cycle provides entanglement propagation similar to a ring interaction, suitable for detecting global connectivity properties.

proposals.note: Designed a block invariant under the dihedral group D6 (rotations and reflections of the hexagon graph). The graph connectivity task is invariant under node relabeling (isomorphism), and the D6 subgroup of S6 is a natural symmetry of the 6-node ring structure often used in graph embeddings. The block uses uniform single-qubit rotations (RZ, RX) and entangling CZ gates arranged in a ring (nearest neighbors) and a second layer of next-nearest neighbors (distance 2). The CZ gates are symmetric under the generators (rotation [1,2,3,4,5,0] and reflection [1,0,3,2,5,4]). The rotation generator maps edges (i, i+1) to (i+1, i+2) and (i, i+2) to (i+1, i+3), preserving the set of applied gates. The reflection generator maps edges (i, i+1) to (5-i, 4-i) which are also nearest neighbors, and (i, i+2) to (5-i, 3-i) which are also distance-2 neighbors. This structure is highly constrained (only 2 parameters) but respects the graph isomorphism symmetry, potentially improving generalization and reducing overfitting compared to unconstrained ansatzes. The previous verifier report indicated a failure in equivariance for a different hypothesis; this proposal strictly enforces D6 symmetry on the gate structure itself.

proposals.note: Proposed a highly symmetric ansatz block with 24 gates and 3 parameters. The structure consists of uniform single-qubit rotations (RX, RY) on all qubits, followed by a ring of CZ gates connecting nearest neighbors in a cycle (0-1-2-3-4-5-0), and finally uniform RZ rotations. This structure is explicitly invariant under the dihedral group D6 (generated by cyclic shift and reflection), which matches the symmetry of the graph connectivity task. The previous verifier failure indicated that the claimed invariance was not realized by the gate list; this block enforces the symmetry by using identical parameters for all qubits in each rotation layer and a symmetric entangling topology. The low parameter count (3) and high symmetry aim to reduce overfitting and align with the structural bias of the problem.

proposals.note: Designed a block with D6 dihedral symmetry (rotation + reflection) to match the graph isomorphism invariance of the connectivity problem. The block consists of two layers of CZ entanglers: the first layer forms a cycle (edges of a hexagon), and the second layer forms a second cycle (chords of a hexagon, effectively a second Hamiltonian cycle). These two sets of edges are invariant under the dihedral group D6 acting on the 6 nodes. The single-qubit rotations are uniform across all qubits (tied parameters p0, p1), preserving the symmetry. This structure allows the ansatz to learn features dependent on global graph properties (like connectivity) while being invariant to node relabeling, reducing the hypothesis space and potentially improving generalization.

proposals.note: Design leverages the cyclic symmetry of the ring topology implied by the graph connectivity task. The block consists of a uniform layer of Hadamard gates, a ring of CZ gates, a uniform layer of RX rotations with a single shared parameter, and a second ring of CZ gates. This structure is invariant under the cyclic permutation of qubits (generator [1,2,3,4,5,0]), which corresponds to the rotational symmetry of the 6-node cycle. The CZ gates are symmetric under this permutation, and the uniform single-qubit rotations preserve the symmetry. This reduces the parameter space to 1 trainable parameter per block, minimizing overfitting risk while capturing the structural invariance of the connectivity problem.

proposals.note: The task (graph connectivity) is invariant under node permutation. The previous proposal failed because the claimed symmetry group (order 6) was not realized by the gate structure (high residual). This proposal uses a cyclic shift generator (0->1->...->5->0) and constructs a block that is explicitly equivariant under this permutation: it applies identical single-qubit rotations (tied parameters) to all qubits and applies entangling gates (CZ) on all edges of the cycle graph (0-1, 1-2, ..., 5-0). This structure ensures that permuting the qubits corresponds to a symmetry of the circuit, satisfying the equivariance condition. The tied parameters reduce the search space and enforce the symmetry. The block is repeated 2 times as required.
